````text
# #4024: Patch: the AI prices each side's copy of a card's Death and turn hooks on its own board, as it already does Activates
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Before it decides, the practice AI works out what a card's “when this dies” text and its start- or end-of-turn text are worth. It does this once per card. When both players have the same card, it reuses one side's figure for the other side's copy, though the same text is worth very different amounts on different boards.

Jlockeed Shredder-10 deals 2 to each enemy unit at the end of its turn. On the AI's side, facing a full board, it is worth a lot; on the opponent's side, facing the AI's empty board, it is worth little. The AI prices both copies the same. Floodgates (“Death: destroy all your Units”) is worse: a copy in the AI's hand can borrow the near-zero figure of the opponent's copy on an empty board. Both players hold the same card in mirror matchups, with tokens both sides make, and after copy and steal effects. Once built, each side's copy is priced on its own board, as the AI already prices activated abilities.

## Why
- `ActivationPrice` keys on the controller, with the reason written down: “The controller is in the key since each copy aims at a different board” (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:355-380`).
- `DeathPrice::is_for` (`evaluate.rs:208-213`) and `TurnHookPrice::is_for` (`:265-267`) match only the definition and the face.
- `death_prices` (from `:1617`) and `turn_hook_prices` (from `:1889`) probe each card once, skipping any card whose key is already listed. The order is the seat's field, then the enemy's field and readable backrow, then the seat's hand. So an enemy copy takes the price of the seat's field copy, and a hand copy takes the price of the enemy's field copy.
- Cards affected include Core #13 Jlockeed Shredder-10, TG #30 Floodgates, S #49 Spacemine, C+ #3 Second Amendment Snake, and any token made on both sides.

## Proposal
1. Add `controller` to `DeathPrice` and `TurnHookPrice`, in their `key` and `is_for`, as `ActivationPrice` has it. A stolen copy then finds no price until the next root probes it, which is how activations already behave.
2. Keep the probes within `AI_DEATH_PROBE_NODES` and `AI_TURN_HOOK_PROBE_NODES`. A mirror now probes twice. The seat's own copies still go first, so a tight budget is spent where the AI acts.
3. Reword the two probes' doc comments (“each card once”) to match.

## Where it lands
- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, and any test literal of the two price structs
- SPEC §9.9 needs no change.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Shredder-10 on both sides facing unequal boards: `turn_hook_prices` returns two entries with different prices, and the enemy copy reads the enemy-side probe.
- [ ] Floodgates on the enemy's empty board and in the AI's hand: `death_prices` prices them apart, and the AI's copy is priced below zero while its side has units.
- [ ] The existing price tests and `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke) pass, and the timing gate holds.

## Size and risks
Small: about 20 lines plus tests. Hard by label (the AI). The risk is more probe nodes in mirror positions, which the budgets cap.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-8` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43789254457)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Key the AI's Death prices and turn-hook prices by the controller of the card, as `ActivationPrice` is. Each side's copy of a card then gets its own probe. Both `DeathPrice::key`/`is_for` and `TurnHookPrice::key`/`is_for` gain `controller`, and the two doc comments that say "each card once" are reworded.

- **Acceptance 1:** `turn_hook_prices` returns two entries with different prices for Shredder-10 on both sides facing unequal boards. The enemy copy reads the enemy-side probe.
- **Acceptance 2:** `death_prices` prices Floodgates apart on the enemy's empty board and in the AI's hand. The AI's copy is below zero while its side has units.
- **Acceptance 3:** the existing price tests and `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke) pass, and the probes stay within `AI_DEATH_PROBE_NODES` and `AI_TURN_HOOK_PROBE_NODES`.

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs` | change: add `controller: PlayerId` to `DeathPrice` and `TurnHookPrice`. Set it in both `key` fns and test it in both `is_for` fns. Reword the doc comments of `death_prices` and `turn_hook_prices`. |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/deaths.rs` | change: add `controller` to the `DeathPrice` literal (~line 542). Add the Floodgates test and a `price_for` helper. |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/turn_hooks.rs` | change: add `controller` to the two `TurnHookPrice` literals (~lines 174 and 392). Rewrite the "both sides" part of `r2565000_a_unit_with_a_turn_hook_is_priced_on_either_field`. Add the Shredder-10 test and a `price_for` helper. |
| `crates/ai/README.md` | change: lines ~128–146, add that a Death and a turn-hook price is kept per controller, so each side's copy is probed on its own board. |
| `spec/rulings/R4024000.md` | new: the ruling note. |
| `spec/pending/4024.md` | new: the ruling's §11 paragraph. |

Do not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, and `spec/09-architecture.md` (the issue says §9.9 needs no change). Never run `cargo jackioh spec index`.

Governing rulings: R2424000, R2687000 (Death prices), R2477000, R2565000, R2689000 (turn-hook prices), R2564000 (the `ActivationPrice` precedent), CLAUDE.md rules 3 and 9. No `.rs` file under `crates/` outside `crates/ai` constructs the two structs (grep confirmed; only `spec/rulings/*.md` mention them), and no number is new.

## Steps

1. **`DeathPrice`** (`evaluate.rs` ~188).
   - Add the field `pub controller: PlayerId` between `stats_override` and `price`. Add a doc line: "the controller is in the key since each copy aims at a different board".
   - In `key`, set `controller: card.controller`.
   - In `is_for`, add `&& self.controller == card.controller`.
   - Update the struct's doc comment (~183) to list the controller among the card facts.
2. **`TurnHookPrice`** (`evaluate.rs` ~246).
   - Add `pub controller: PlayerId` after `radiant`. Set it in `key` and test it in `is_for`, as `ActivationPrice` does at ~365–378.
   - Update the doc comment (~242) to say "its definition, its face and its controller".
3. **`death_prices`** (~1683). The dedupe `candidates.iter().any(|(key, _, _)| key.is_for(card))` needs no edit; it now keys on the controller.
   - Order is unchanged: the seat's field, then the enemy's field, then backrow, then hand. A hand card's controller equals the seat (`zones.rs:1238` resets it to the owner), so a hand copy shares a key with the seat's field copy and is still skipped.
   - Reword the doc (~1676–1682): "each card once" becomes "each card once per controller, so each side's copy is priced on its own board; the seat's own cards first, so a tight budget is spent where the AI acts".
4. **`turn_hook_prices`** (~1954). The dedupe at ~1996 is also unchanged. Reword the doc (~1948–1953) the same way.
5. **Other users of `Prices.deaths` / `Prices.turn_hooks`.** `death_price` (~227) and `turn_hook_price` (~339) call `is_for`, which now matches the controller, so no edit is needed.
   - A stolen or controlled-by-other copy finds no entry and reads 0 until the next root probes it. This matches activations. Say so in the ruling.
6. **Existing tests that stop compiling or asserting.**
   - `deaths.rs` `DeathPrice { … }` at ~542: add `controller: HUMAN`. The card is the enemy's Sheepish.
   - `turn_hooks.rs` ~174: add `controller: AI`. The held trap sits on the AI's own backrow (the second eval uses `own`).
   - `turn_hooks.rs` ~392: add `controller: HUMAN`. The trap is the enemy's.
   - `turn_hooks.rs` `r2565000_a_unit_with_a_turn_hook_is_priced_on_either_field`, the `both` block (~313–324): it now expects `prices.len() == 2` and `used == 2`, since each side's Gatling Pea is probed. Change the message to "each side's copy is priced on its own board". Also assert `prices[0].controller == AI` and `prices[1].controller == HUMAN`, the seat's own first.
7. **New helpers.** In each of the two test files add, next to `price_of`:
   ```rust
   fn price_for(prices: &[DeathPrice], def_id: &str, controller: PlayerId) -> f64 // TurnHookPrice + radiant in turn_hooks.rs
   ```
   It finds the entry by `def_id` and `controller` and panics with `{prices:?}` if missing. The existing `price_of` stays.
8. **Ruling.**
   - Create `spec/rulings/R4024000.md`, modelled on `spec/rulings/R2689000.md`. Front matter:
     - `id: R4024000`
     - a `title`: "The AI prices each side's copy of a card's Death and turn hooks on its own board (issue #4024; amends R2424000, R2477000)"
     - `cards: "§9.9, R2424000, R2477000, R2564000, R2565000, R2687000, R2689000; Core #13; TG #30"`
     - `proven_in`: `crates/ai/tests/ai/deaths.rs` and `crates/ai/tests/ai/turn_hooks.rs`
   - Body, in order:
     - **Problem:** `DeathPrice` and `TurnHookPrice` matched only definition and face, so an enemy copy took the seat's field copy's price and a hand copy took the enemy field copy's. Name Shredder-10 and Floodgates.
     - **Change:** the controller joins the key, and the seat's own copies are still probed first.
     - **Stolen copy:** it reads 0 until the next root probes it.
     - **Budget:** the node caps are unchanged. A mirror probes twice, and the order spends a tight budget on the seat's side first.
     - **Rejected:** keying by owner instead of controller, because a stolen copy would keep a price from the wrong board; and raising the caps, because the caps are what hold the timing gate.
   - Create `spec/pending/4024.md` with one paragraph beginning `**[[R4024000]] <title> (issue #4024, 2026-11-16; amends [[R2424000]], [[R2477000]])**: …`, in the style of `spec/pending/3937.md`.
9. **README.** Edit `crates/ai/README.md` ~128 and ~139. After "each live Death on the field and in the seat's hand" add "(per controller: each side's copy is probed on its own board, R4024000)". Add the same for the turn hooks.

## Tests

New tests, named after the ruling and listed in `proven_in`:

- **`deaths.rs`: `r4024000_a_floodgates_is_priced_on_its_own_board_for_each_side`.**
  - Setup: `sides("ai-death-mirror", json!({ "hand": [FLOODGATES], "field": [VANILLA, VANILLA] }), json!({ "field": [FLOODGATES] }))`.
  - Assert `prices.len() == 2`.
  - Assert `price_for(.., FLOODGATES, AI) < 0.0` (the hand copy destroys the AI's two Vanillas).
  - Assert `price_for(.., FLOODGATES, HUMAN) > price_for(.., FLOODGATES, AI)`. The enemy's board is otherwise empty, so its Death costs little. Run once and print the values first; if the enemy copy comes out below zero, pick a setup where it does not.
  - Assert `used <= AI_DEATH_PROBE_NODES`.
  - Assert the order is `[HUMAN, AI]` (field before hand).
  - Also assert `unit_worth` of the enemy's Floodgates, passed `prices_of(prices)`, differs from the same call with the entry's price swapped for the AI copy's. This shows each side reads its own entry.
- **`turn_hooks.rs`: `r4024000_a_shredder_on_each_side_is_priced_on_the_board_it_hits`.**
  - Add `const SHREDDER_10: &str = "core-013";`.
  - Setup: `sides("ai-hook-shredder", json!({ "field": [SHREDDER_10] }), json!({ "field": [SHREDDER_10, VANILLA, VANILLA, VANILLA] }))`. The AI's Shredder faces a full enemy board; the enemy's faces only the AI's own Shredder.
  - Assert `prices.len() == 2`.
  - Assert `price_for(.., AI) > price_for(.., HUMAN)`, and that they differ by more than 1e-9.
  - Assert `used <= AI_TURN_HOOK_PROBE_NODES`.
  - If the numbers do not separate, make the AI's board empty and the enemy's side hold the units until they do.
- **`turn_hooks.rs`: the rewritten `both` block** from step 6.
- **`deaths.rs`: `r4024000_a_copy_under_the_other_controller_reads_no_price`.**
  - Use the setup above. Take the enemy's Floodgates `unit(&state, HUMAN, FLOODGATES)` and clone it with `controller = AI`.
  - Call `unit_worth` with the priced deaths filtered to the HUMAN-controller entry only. It must equal the `Prices::NONE` worth, since no entry matches.

Run, in this order:
```
cargo test -p jackioh-ai r4024000
cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai deaths
cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai turn_hooks
cargo test -p jackioh-ai
cargo jackioh spec check
cargo jackioh gate
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings
```
If another test in `crates/ai` fails because a mirror now yields two entries or more nodes, fix its expectation to the new rule; do not loosen it. Every such change has its reason in the ruling.

## Done when

- [ ] Both price structs carry `controller` in `key` and `is_for`; both probe doc comments are reworded.
- [ ] Acceptance 1 and 2 are asserted by tests that fail on the old code.
- [ ] R4024000 and `spec/pending/4024.md` exist, with tests named `r4024000_…` listed in `proven_in`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` is green.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke) passes, including its timing part.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` is run. If it demands a patch fragment for the AI change, add it as `cargo jackioh patches "<title>" --rule` says.
- [ ] No `#[ignore]`, `#[allow]`, deleted test or raised cap anywhere in the diff.
- [ ] The harness checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests, web tests.

## Risks

- **Probe budget.** Mirror positions probe twice. The caps (24 nodes each) are unchanged, and the seat's own copies are probed first, so a cut-off drops the enemy's copy. If a test's crowded board (`r2565000_the_probes_of_two_crowded_boards…`, `r2687000_backrow_deaths_follow…`) now changes its priced list, check the counts. Those tests assert `used <= cap` and order.
- **Timing and strength gates.** `cargo jackioh gate` smoke is the check. If it fails on timing, do not raise any constant. Report it with the output.
- **Determinism.** Probes stay on the sandbox clone with the state's own rng, so nothing in replay or hidden information changes. The hand probe reads only the seat's own hand.
- **Evaluation-parity fixtures.** If a fixture under `crates/ai/tests/fixtures/` or a shadow report of record changes (`crates/ai/src/shadow_ban.rs`), regenerate it only if its own README says so; otherwise report it.
- **Purity.** The change adds a `PlayerId` field and no clock, I/O or hash-ordered collection (CLAUDE.md rule 4).

## Open questions

- None that block the build. The issue asks for no spec change, but an AI-behaviour change in this repo carries a ruling note (precedent: R2689000, R3937000), so the plan adds R4024000.
- Rated hard.
````

Key the AI's Death prices and turn-hook prices by the controller of the card, as `ActivationPrice` is. Each side's copy of a card then gets its own probe. Both `DeathPrice::key`/`is_for` and `TurnHookPrice::key`/`is_for` gain `controller`, and the two doc comments that say "each card once" are reworded.

- **Acceptance 1:** `turn_hook_prices` returns two entries with different prices for Shredder-10 on both sides facing unequal boards. The enemy copy reads the enemy-side probe.
- **Acceptance 2:** `death_prices` prices Floodgates apart on the enemy's empty board and in the AI's hand. The AI's copy is below zero while its side has units.
- **Acceptance 3:** the existing price tests and `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke) pass, and the probes stay within `AI_DEATH_PROBE_NODES` and `AI_TURN_HOOK_PROBE_NODES`.
